claim: During the development of the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans, many somatic and germ cells undergo apoptosis.
source: During the development of the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans, many somatic and germ cells undergo apoptosis.
evidence: This is a well-established fact about C. elegans development, supported by citations in the manuscript (Sulston and Horvitz, 1977; Sulston et al., 1980; Gumienny et al., 1999).

claim: Double-membrane autophagosomes in engulfing cells are recruited to the surfaces of phagosomes containing apoptotic cells.
source: Specifically, the double-membrane autophagosomes in engulfing cells are recruited to the surfaces of phagosomes containing apoptotic cells and subsequently fuse to phagosomes, allowing the inner vesicle to enter the phagosomal lumen.
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing LGG-labeled puncta enriched on phagosomal surfaces (Figures 1, 8).

claim: Autophagosomes fuse to phagosomes, allowing the inner vesicle to enter the phagosomal lumen.
source: Specifically, the double-membrane autophagosomes in engulfing cells are recruited to the surfaces of phagosomes containing apoptotic cells and subsequently fuse to phagosomes, allowing the inner vesicle to enter the phagosomal lumen.
evidence: This is demonstrated by mCherry::LGG signal accumulating inside the phagosomal lumen over time (Figures 1E, F, H, I).

claim: Mutants defective in the production of autophagosomes display significant defects in the degradation of apoptotic cells.
source: Mutants defective in the production of autophagosomes display significant defects in the degradation of apoptotic cells, demonstrating the importance of autophagosomes to this process.
evidence: This is supported by data showing increased cell corpse numbers in atg-7, atg-9, atg-13, and epg-8 mutants (Figure 5) and prolonged phagosome lifespans (Figure 6).

claim: The signaling pathway led by CED-1, CED-6, and DYN-1 promotes the recruitment of autophagosomes to phagosomes.
source: The signaling pathway led by the phagocytic receptor CED-1, the adaptor protein CED-6, and the large GTPase dynamin (DYN-1) promotes the recruitment of autophagosomes to phagosomes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by severe defects in autophagosome recruitment to phagosomes in ced-1, ced-6, and dyn-1 mutants (Figures 9, 10).

claim: The fusion of autophagosomes with phagosomes requires the functions of RAB-7 and the HOPS complex.
source: Moreover, the subsequent fusion of autophagosomes with phagosomes requires the functions of the small GTPase RAB-7 and the HOPS complex.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that in rab-7 and vps-18 mutants, autophagosomes are recruited to phagosomes but fail to fuse (Figure 8G-J).

claim: Autophagosomes provide apoptotic cell-degradation activities in addition to and in parallel with lysosomes.
source: Further observations suggest that autophagosomes provide apoptotic cell-degradation activities in addition to and in parallel of lysosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from data showing that lysosome-phagosome fusion is not significantly affected in autophagy mutants (Figure 11), and that rab-7 mutants (which block both lysosome and autophagosome fusion) have more severe defects than autophagy mutants alone (Figure 6).

claim: It is the canonical double-membrane autophagosomes, not single-membrane LAP vesicles, that facilitate the clearance of C. elegans apoptotic cells.
source: Our findings reveal that, unlike the single-membrane, LC3-associated phagocytosis (LAP) vesicles reported to facilitate phagocytosis in mammals, it is the canonical double-membrane autophagosomes that facilitate the clearance of C. elegans apoptotic cells.
evidence: This is supported by multiple lines of evidence: (1) mCherry::LGG signal enters the phagosomal lumen, which is only possible with double-membrane vesicles (Figure 1K); (2) LGG+ vesicles are also labeled with ATG-9 (Figure 3); (3) TEM images show double-membrane vesicles on phagosomal surfaces (Figure 4); (4) production of these vesicles requires atg-13 and epg-8, which are dispensable for LAP vesicles (Figure 2).

claim: During C. elegans embryonic development, 131 somatic cells undergo apoptosis and are swiftly engulfed and degraded by neighboring cells.
source: During C. elegans embryonic development, 131 somatic cells undergo apoptosis and are swiftly engulfed and degraded by neighboring cells (Sulston and Horvitz, 1977; Sulston et al., 1980).
evidence: This is established knowledge about C. elegans development, supported by the cited references.

claim: In the C. elegans hermaphrodite gonad, 300–500 germ cells undergo apoptosis and are cleared by the neighboring gonadal sheath cells.
source: In the C. elegans hermaphrodite gonad, 300–500 germ cells undergo apoptosis and are cleared by the neighboring gonadal sheath cells (Gumienny et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge about C. elegans germ cell death, supported by the cited reference.

claim: C. elegans has two LC3/GABARAP family members, LGG-1 and LGG-2, which belong to the LC3 and GABARAP subfamilies, respectively.
source: C. elegans has two LC3/GABARAP family members, LGG-1 and LGG-2, which belong to the LC3 and GABARAP subfamilies, respectively (Figure 1A; Manil-Ségalen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by Figure 1A showing domain structures and by the cited reference.

claim: Both LGG-1 and LGG-2 are attached to autophagosomes, except they each label autophagosomes of different maturity.
source: Both LGG-1 and LGG-2 are attached to autophagosomes, except they each label autophagosomes of different maturity (Manil-Ségalen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference and by data showing distinct and overlapping populations of LGG-1+ and LGG-2+ puncta (Figure 7).

claim: GFP::LGG-1+ and GFP::LGG-2+ puncta are enriched to the surfaces of phagosomes containing apoptotic cells C1, C2, and C3.
source: Using our previously established time-lapse recording protocol (Lu et al., 2009), we observed the enrichment of GFP::LGG-1+ and GFP-LGG-2+ puncta to the surfaces of the phagosomes, including the phagosomes containing apoptotic cells C1, C2, and C3 (Figure 1B, D and G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figures 1D and G.

claim: GFP::LGG-1(G116A) and GFP::LGG-2(G130A) display a diffuse cytosolic localization pattern, in contrast to the punctate pattern of GFP::LGG-1 and GFP::LGG-2.
source: We found that both GFP::LGG-1(G116A) and GFP::LGG-2(G130A) display a diffuse cytosolic localization pattern (Figure 1D, G, bottom panels), in stark contrast to the punctate pattern presented by GFP::LGG-1 and GFP::LGG-2.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D and G, demonstrating that the punctate pattern depends on lipidation.

claim: The GFP::LGG-1 and GFP::LGG-2 puncta are membrane-attached and label lipid vesicles.
source: This result indicates that GFP::LGG-1 and::LGG-2 are membrane attached and thus label lipid vesicles.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that mutations in lipidation sites (G116A and G130A) abolish the punctate pattern (Figure 1D, G).

claim: mCherry::LGG and mNG::LGG reporters enter the phagosomal lumen after being recruited to phagosomal surfaces.
source: In time-lapse image series of the clearance process of C1, C2, and C3, we found that like the GFP::LGG reporters, the mCherry::LGG and mNG::LGG reporters were enriched on the surfaces of phagosomes; moreover, unlike the GFP::LGG reporters, the mCherry and mNG-tagged reporters subsequently entered phagosomal lumen (Figure 1E, F, H, I).
evidence: This is demonstrated by time-lapse imaging data in Figures 1E, F, H, and I.

claim: The fluorescence signal intensity of mCherry::LGG-1 and mCherry::LGG-2 in the center of phagosomes increases over 10-fold within 60 min.
source: We measured the intensity of the mCherry::LGG-1 and mCherry::LGG-2 signal in the center of the C3 phagosomes over time from the start of the phagosome (Materials and methods) (Figure 1C) and observed over 10-fold increases of the signal intensity within 60 min (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The appearance of membrane-attached mCherry::LGG and mNG::LGG signal in the phagosomal lumen indicates that the LGG+ vesicles fuse with the phagosomal membrane.
source: The appearance of the membrane-attached mCherry::LGG and mNG::LGG signal in the phagosomal lumen indicates that the LGG+ vesicles fuse with the phagosomal membrane (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that membrane-attached LGG signal accumulates inside the phagosomal lumen, which is only possible through fusion of double-membrane vesicles (Figure 1K).

claim: The LGG+ vesicles that fuse to phagosomes are composed of double membranes labeled with LGG reporter molecules on both the outer and inner membranes.
source: They further suggest that these vesicles are composed of double membranes labeled with the LGG reporter molecules on both the outer and inner membranes (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that LGG signal enters the phagosomal lumen, which would only occur if the vesicles are double-membrane (Figure 1K).

claim: If LGG+ vesicles were single-membrane, no membrane-attached LGG reporter would end up inside the phagosomal lumen after fusion.
source: If these LGG+ vesicles were single-membrane, no membrane-attached LGG reporter would end up inside the phagosomal lumen because, as a result of fusion, the reporter molecules will be retained on the phagosomal membrane (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the mechanism of membrane fusion, illustrated in Figure 1K.

claim: When CTNS-1::mRFP (a lysosomal transmembrane protein) fuses to phagosomes, the mRFP signal is only observed on the phagosomal surface, not in the phagosomal lumen.
source: Indeed, when CTNS-1, a lysosomal transmembrane protein, is tagged with mRFP, which is acid-resistant (pKa = 4.5 [Shaner et al., 2004]), on its C-terminus, the lysosome-phagosome fusion event resulted in the incorporation of the mRFP signal into the phagosomal membrane; as a result, the CTNS-1::mRFP signal is only observed on the phagosomal surface, not in the phagosomal lumen (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Yu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: In C. elegans embryos, LGG-1 or LGG-2-labeled vesicles are double-membrane autophagosomes, as shown by electron microscopy and immuno-gold staining.
source: In support of this model, previously, using electron microscopy and immune-gold staining, Manil-Ségalen et al have shown that in C. elegans embryos, LGG-1 or LGG-2-labeled vesicles are double-membrane autophagosomes (Manil-Ségalen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference using electron microscopy.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations of atg-7, atg-13, and epg-8 impair the production of LGG+ vesicles that fuse to phagosomes.
source: To further determine whether these vesicles represent canonical autophagosomes, we examined whether loss-of-function mutations of atg-7, atg-13, and epg-8, which are defective for the biogenesis of autophagosomes (Tian et al., 2010; Yang and Zhang, 2011), impaired the production of these vesicles.
evidence: This is demonstrated by data showing drastically reduced or absent mCherry::LGG signal inside phagosomes in these mutants (Figure 2).

claim: In atg-7(bp411) mutant embryos, hardly any mCherry::LGG signal is observed inside phagosomes.
source: However, in atg-7(bp411) (Gomes et al., 2016) mutant embryos, hardly any mCherry signal was observed inside phagosomes (Figure 2A, D and G–J).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A, D, and G-J.

claim: At 60 min after phagosome formation in atg-7 mutants, the average mCherry::LGG-1 and -LGG-2 signal intensities are merely 1.2 and 1.4-fold of the 0 min time point.
source: At 60 min after the phagosome formation, the average mCherry signal intensities were merely 1.2 and 1.4-fold at 0 min time point (Figure 2H and J).
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 2H and J.

claim: In atg-13(bp414) and epg-8(bp251) mutant embryos, the defects in autophagosome-phagosome fusion are slightly weaker than in atg-7 mutants.
source: In atg-13(bp414) and epg-8(bp251) mutant embryos, similar observations were made except that the defects were slightly weaker (Figure 2B, C, E, F and G–J).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B, C, E, F, and G-J.

claim: In wild-type embryos at mid-embryonic developmental stages, numerous mCherry::LGG-1 and mCherry::LGG-2 puncta are observed.
source: In wild-type embryos at mid-embryonic developmental stages (~330, ~ 350, ~ 400 min post-1st embryonic cell division), numerous mCherry+ puncta were observed (Figure 2—figure supplements 1A and 2A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplements 1A and 2A.

claim: In atg-7 mutant embryos, rarely any mCherry::LGG puncta exist.
source: In the atg-7 mutant embryos, rarely any such puncta existed (Figure 2—figure supplements 1B and 2B), consistent with a previous report (Tian et al., 2010).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplements 1B and 2B and is consistent with the cited reference.

claim: In atg-9(bp564) mutant embryos, much fewer mNG::LGG-1 or mNG::LGG-2 puncta are observed, and the reporters label large aggregates.
source: In atg-9(bp564) mutant embryos that expressed mNG::LGG-1 or::LGG-2, much fewer mNG+ puncta that might represent autophagosomes were observed, and the mNG reporters label large aggregates (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), consistent with a previous report (Lin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and is consistent with the cited reference.

claim: In atg-13 and epg-8 mutant embryos, the numbers of mCherry::LGG+ puncta are significantly reduced.
source: In atg-13 and epg-8 mutant embryos, the numbers of mCherry-LGG+ puncta were also significantly reduced (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C-D), suggesting that the atg-13(bp414) and epn-8(bp251) mutations severely impaired the biogenesis of autophagosomes, a phenotype that is consistent with previous reports (Tian et al., 2010; Yang and Zhang, 2011).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplements 1C-D and 2C-D and is consistent with the cited references.

claim: The drastic reduction in the number of LGG-1/–2-labeled puncta in atg-7, atg-9, atg-13, and epg-8 loss-of-function mutants strongly indicates that these puncta belong to canonical autophagosomes.
source: The drastic reduction in the number of LGG-1/–2-labeled puncta in atg-7, atg-9, atg-13, and epg-8 loss-of-function mutants strongly indicates that these puncta belong to canonical autophagosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that genes essential for autophagosome biogenesis are required for the production of these puncta (Figures 2, 3—figure supplement 1).

claim: mCherry::ATG-9 puncta are recruited to the surfaces of phagosomes and the mCherry signal gradually accumulates in the phagosomal lumen.
source: In embryonic hypodermal cells that co-expressed mCherry::ATG-9 and either mNG::LGG-1 or::LGG-2, puncta labeled with mCherry are recruited to the surfaces of phagosomes (Figure 3). Furthermore, the mCherry signal gradually accumulates in the phagosomal lumen like the LGG reporters (Figure 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by time-lapse imaging data in Figure 3.

claim: The co-localization between mCherry::ATG-9 and mNG::LGG-1 or mNG::LGG-2 on puncta on phagosomal surfaces and inside phagosomal lumen is nearly perfect.
source: During the phagosome maturation process, the co-localization between mCherry::ATG-9 and each of the two LGG reporters on the puncta on phagosomal surfaces and inside phagosomal lumen was nearly perfect (Figure 3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3.

claim: ATG-9 and LGG double-positive autophagosomes are recruited to phagosomal surfaces and subsequently fuse to phagosomes containing apoptotic cells.
source: Together, the above observations verified that the ATG-9 and LGG double-positive autophagosomes are recruited to phagosomal surfaces and subsequently fuse to phagosomes containing apoptotic cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-localization data and the accumulation of both markers inside the phagosomal lumen (Figure 3).

claim: The recruitment of mCherry::LGG-1 or -2 to phagosomes and the subsequent entry of the mCherry signal to the phagosomal lumen is observed in multiple phagosomes in embryos.
source: Besides the C1, C2, and C3 phagosomes, in embryos co-expressing mCherry::LGG-1 or –2 and CED-1::GFP reporters, we also observed the recruitment of the mCherry signal to other phagosomes and the subsequent entry of the mCherry signal to the phagosomal lumen (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-E.

claim: The fusion between autophagosomes and phagosomes is a general phenomenon during embryogenesis.
source: These observations indicate that the fusion between autophagosomes and phagosomes is a general phenomenon during embryogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from observations of autophagosome-phagosome fusion in multiple phagosomes beyond C1, C2, and C3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).

claim: In rab-7(ok511) mutant adult gonads, multiple double-membrane vesicles are in close contact with phagosomal surfaces.
source: In rab-7 mutant gonad, we did identify multiple double-membrane vesicles in close contact with the phagosomal surfaces in TEM thin sections (Figure 4D–H).
evidence: This is shown in TEM images in Figure 4D-H.

claim: The double-membrane vesicles observed on phagosomal surfaces in rab-7 mutant gonad resemble autophagosomes identified in C. elegans cells.
source: Besides being composed of double membranes, these vesicles also resemble autophagosomes identified in C. elegans cells (Kovacs et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on comparison with autophagosomes described in the cited references.

claim: The double-membrane vesicles on phagosomal surfaces vary in diameter from 200 nm to 800 nm, consistent with the size of autophagosomes reported in the literature.
source: These vesicles vary in diameter from 200 nm to 800 nm, consistent with that of autophagosomes reported in the literature (Kovacs et al., 2013; Manil-Ségalen et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2015 ).
evidence: This is based on measurements from TEM images (Figure 4) and comparison with the cited references.

claim: The autophagosome-phagosome interaction is general rather than a cell-specific phenomenon.
source: The above observations support our conclusion that the LGG+ puncta that are recruited to phagosomal surfaces are indeed canonical autophagosomes. They further suggest that the autophagosome-phagosome interaction is general rather than a cell-specific phenomenon.
evidence: This is inferred from observations in both embryonic hypodermal cells and adult gonadal sheath cells (Figures 1-4).

claim: Mutant twofold stage embryos of atg-7, atg-9, atg-13, epg-8, lgg-1, lgg-2, atg-3, atg-2, atg-18, and unc-51 bear 46.9–91.2% more cell corpses than wild-type embryos.
source: The mutant twofold stage embryos examined bore 46.9–91.2% more cell corpses (Figure 5), indicating that the clearance of cell corpses is defective.
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 5.

claim: Autophagosomes make a substantial contribution to the clearance of cell corpses.
source: Together, the findings reported in Figures 2—5 indicate that autophagosomes made a substantial contribution to the clearance of cell corpses.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased cell corpse numbers in autophagy mutants (Figure 5) and the defects in autophagosome-phagosome fusion (Figure 2).

claim: In atg-7, lgg-1, and lgg-2 mutant strains, engulfment is completed in 4–8 min, just like in wild-type embryos.
source: In atg-7, lgg-1, and lgg-2 mutant strains that co-expressed CED-1::GFP and 2xFYVE::mRFP, we found that engulfment was completed in 4–8 min, just like in wild-type embryos (Figure 6A–D and F), indicating that defects in autophagosomes biogenesis do not affect the engulfment of cell corpses.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6A-D and F.

claim: The lifespans of phagosomes are much longer in atg-7, lgg-1, and lgg-2 mutants than in wild-type embryos.
source: However, the lifespans of phagosomes (Materials and methods) were much longer in atg-7, lgg-1, and lgg-2 mutants than in wild-type embryos (Figure 6A–D and G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6A-D and G.

claim: All wild-type phagosomes have a lifespan between 40–60 min.
source: All wild-type phagosomes have a lifespan between 40–60 min (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6G.

claim: In atg-7, lgg-1, and lgg-2 mutants, 43.8%, 82.4%, and 53.3% of phagosomes, respectively, have lifespans longer than 60 min.
source: Remarkably, 43.8%, 82.4%, and 53.3% of phagosomes in atg-7, lgg-1, and lgg-2 mutant embryos, respectively, have lifespans longer than 60 min (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Autophagosomes make a specific contribution to the efficient degradation of phagosomal contents.
source: These observations indicate that autophagosomes made a specific contribution to the efficient degradation of phagosomal contents.
evidence: This is inferred from the prolonged phagosome lifespans in autophagy mutants without affecting engulfment (Figure 6).

claim: In lgg-1; lgg-2 double mutant embryos at the twofold stage, the number of cell corpses is 22.0% and 27.1% larger than in the lgg-1 and lgg-2 single mutants, respectively.
source: Furthermore, in lgg-1; lgg-2 double mutant embryos at the twofold stage, the Ced phenotype is further enhanced significantly (Figure 5B) -- the number of cell corpses is 22.0% and 27.1% larger than in the lgg-1 and lgg-2 single mutants, respectively.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The enhanced Ced phenotype in lgg-1; lgg-2 double mutants indicates an additive effect and suggests that autophagosomes labeled with LGG-1 or LGG-2 play parallel and partially redundant roles in promoting phagosome degradation.
source: This enhanced phenotype indicates an additive effect and suggests that the autophagosomes labeled with LGG-1 or LGG-2 play parallel and partially redundant roles in promoting phagosome degradation.
evidence: This is inferred from the additive increase in cell corpse numbers in the double mutant (Figure 5B).

claim: In embryos co-expressing GFP::LGG-1 and mCherry::LGG-2, puncta are observed that are labeled with GFP alone, mCherry alone, or both GFP and mCherry.
source: In embryos co-expressing GFP::LGG-1 and mCherry::LGG-2, we observed that both in the cytoplasm of the engulfing cells and on the surfaces of phagosomes, puncta that were either labeled with GFP or mCherry alone or with both GFP and mCherry (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: In hypodermal cells, the average distribution of LGG-1+ LGG-2-, LGG-1- LGG-2+, and LGG-1+ LGG-2+ puncta is 35.8%, 40.7%, and 23.5%, respectively.
source: In hypodermal cells, the average distribution of LGG-1+ LGG-2-, LGG-1- LGG-2+, and LGG-1+ LGG-2+ puncta is 35.8%, 40.7%, and 23.5%, respectively (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: A third, LGG-1+ LGG-2+ double-positive sub-population of autophagosomes exists, which likely corresponds to an intermediate stage in the maturation path of autophagosomes.
source: These observations indicate that in addition to the LGG-1+-only and LGG-2+-only sub-populations, a third, LGG-1+ LGG-2+ double-positive sub-population of autophagosomes exists. This sub-population likely corresponds to an intermediate stage in the maturation path of autophagosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of three distinct populations of LGG-labeled puncta (Figure 7).

claim: lgg-1 and lgg-2 primarily act in engulfing cells to facilitate the clearance of apoptotic cells.
source: These results indicate that lgg-1 and lgg-2 primarily act in engulfing cells to facilitate the clearance of apoptotic cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the rescue of the Ced phenotype when lgg-1 or lgg-2 is expressed specifically in engulfing cells under Pced-1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

claim: GFP::RAB-7 is localized to some but not all of the LGG-1+ or LGG-2+ puncta.
source: We observed that GFP::RAB-7 was localized to some but not all of the LGG-1+ or LGG-2+ puncta (Figure 8B–D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8B-D.

claim: On average, 66.2% and 63.5% of LGG-1+ and LGG-2+ puncta observed in the cytoplasm of engulfing cells are RAB-7+, respectively.
source: Quantitative analysis of the green and red puncta distribution reveals that on average, 66.2% and 63.5% of LGG-1+ and LGG-2+ puncta observed in the cytoplasm of the engulfing cells are RAB-7+, respectively (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 8E.

claim: 100% of the autophagosomes observed on phagosomal surfaces are RAB-7+.
source: Different from the observation made in the cytoplasm, 100% of the autophagosomes that were observed on phagosomal surfaces were RAB-7+ (Figure 8B, D and F).
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 8F.

claim: RAB-7 might play an essential role in the interaction between autophagosomes and phagosomes.
source: This observation suggests that RAB-7 might play an essential role in the interaction between autophagosomes and phagosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that all autophagosomes on phagosomal surfaces are RAB-7+ (Figure 8F).

claim: In rab-7(ok511) mutant embryos, robust enrichment of both mCherry::LGG-1+ and mCherry::LGG-2+ puncta to phagosomal surfaces is prominent, indicating that the recruitment of autophagosomes is normal.
source: In rab-7(ok511)(m-z-) mutant embryos produced by rab-7(ok511)(m+z-) mothers, robust enrichment of both the mCherry::LGG-1+ and::LGG-2+ puncta to phagosomal surfaces are prominent (Figure 8G–H), indicating that the recruitment of autophagosomes was normal.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8G-H.

claim: In rab-7(ok511) mutant embryos, no mCherry::LGG signal is observed entering the phagosomal lumen.
source: However, no mCherry signal was observed entering the phagosomal lumen (Figure 8G–H, Figure 8—videos 1; 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8G-H and Figure 8—videos 1-2.

claim: In rab-7 mutants, the mCherry::LGG signal is not detected in the lumen of any phagosomes over a time span of 0–60 min after phagosome formation.
source: In stark contrast, in rab-7 mutants, the mCherry signal was not detected in the lumen inside any of the phagosomes for LGG-1 or LGG-2 reporters over a time span of 0–60 min after phagosome formation (Figure 8I–J).
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 8I-J.

claim: RAB-7 is essential for autophagosome-phagosome fusion but not required for the recruitment of autophagosomes to phagosomal surfaces.
source: These results strongly indicate that the function of RAB-7 is essential for autophagosome-phagosome fusion but not required for the recruitment of autophagosomes to phagosomal surfaces.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that in rab-7 mutants, autophagosomes are recruited to phagosomes but do not fuse (Figure 8G-J).

claim: In vps-18 mutants, the recruitment of autophagosomes to phagosomes appears normal.
source: We found that, like in rab-7 mutants, the recruitment of autophagosomes to phagosomes appeared normal in vps-18 mutants (Figure 8G–H).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8G-H.

claim: In vps-18 mutants, the fusion of LGG-1+ and LGG-2+ autophagosomes to phagosomes is severely defective.
source: Also, like in rab-7 mutants, in vps-18 mutants, the fusion of LGG-1+ and LGG-2+ autophagosomes to phagosomes was severely defective (Figure 8G–J).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8G-J.

claim: In vps-18 mutants, the fusion defect is less severe than that caused by the rab-7 null mutation.
source: However, whereas in rab-7 mutants, the accumulation of the mCherry signal in the phagosomal lumen was blocked completely in all samples, in some vps-18 mutant embryos, the entry of mCherry signal still occurred, albeit severely delayed (Figure 8I–J). In contrast, in other samples, the entry was blocked (Figure 8I–J), indicating a fusion defect that is less severe than that caused by the rab-7 null mutation and suggesting the existence of the residual HOPS function in vps-18 mutants.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8I-J.

claim: RAB-7 and the HOPS complex play a critical and specific role in driving the fusion between autophagosomes and phagosomes.
source: Together, our observations indicate that RAB-7 and the HOPS complex play a critical and specific role in driving the fusion between autophagosomes and phagosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the severe fusion defects observed in rab-7 and vps-18 mutants (Figure 8G-J).

claim: In rab-7 mutants, 100% of phagosomes last longer than 60 min, among which 71.4% last longer than 80 min and 57% last longer than 90 min.
source: In rab-7 mutants, 100% of phagosomes last longer than 60 min, among which 71.4% last longer than 80 min and 57% last longer than 90 min (Figure 6E and G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6E and G.

claim: The difference in severity in phagosome degradation defects between rab-7 and autophagy mutants suggests that autophagosomes and lysosomes both contribute to phagosome degradation, and that autophagosomes provide a phagosome degradation activity in an additive and possibly independent manner to lysosomes.
source: The difference in severity in the phagosome degradation defects displayed by rab-7 and autophagy mutants suggest that autophagosomes and lysosomes both contribute to phagosome degradation, and that autophagosomes provide a phagosome degradation activity in an additive and possibly independent manner to lysosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the phagosome lifespans in rab-7 mutants (which block both lysosome and autophagosome fusion) versus autophagy mutants (which only block autophagosome fusion) (Figure 6).

claim: In ced-1(e1735) mutants, only a very dim mNG::LGG signal is observed inside the phagosomal lumen 50 min post phagosome formation.
source: In ced-1(e1735) mutants expressing the mNG::LGG-1 or –2 reporters, we observed severe defects in the incorporation of autophagosomes into phagosomes. First of all, only a very dim mNG signal was observed inside the phagosomal lumen 50 min post phagosome formation, a time point well past the observed initiation time for autophagosomes/phagosome fusion in the wild-type condition (Figure 9A, C, F and G, Figure 9—video 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9A, C, F, and G.

claim: In wild-type embryos, the median relative LGG-1 and LGG-2 signal intensities are 6.3 and 5.3 at 50 min-post phagosome formation, respectively.
source: Whereas in wild-type embryos, the median relative LGG-1 and –2 signal intensities are 6.3 and 5.3 at 50 min-post phagosome formation, respectively, in ced-1 mutant embryos, the median values are merely 2.1 and 1.6, respectively (Figure 9K–L).
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 9K-L.

claim: In ced-1 mutants, very few LGG-1- or LGG-2-labeled puncta are observed on phagosomal surfaces.
source: Secondly, unlike in rab-7 mutants, where autophagosomes were observed accumulating on phagosomal surfaces (Figure 8G–J), in ced-1 mutants, very few LGG-1- or LGG-2-labeled puncta were observed on phagosomal surfaces (Figure 9A and C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9A and C.

claim: In ced-1 mutants, the mNG signal is not enriched on the surfaces of phagosomes.
source: Further quantitative measurement of the samples presented in (Figure 9A and C) and 14 additional samples for each of the reporters confirmed that the mNG signal was not enriched on the surfaces of phagosomes, in contrast to wild-type embryos (Figure 9H–L).
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 9H-L.

claim: In ced-1 mutants, normal numbers of LGG-1+ or LGG-2+ puncta are observed, indicating that the biogenesis of autophagosomes is normal.
source: Unlike in the atg mutants that we have examined (Figure 2—figure supplements 1–2), in ced-1 mutant embryos, normal numbers of LGG-1+ or LGG-2+ puncta were observed (Figure 9—figure supplement 1), indicating that the biogenesis of autophagosomes is normal.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: The recruitment defect observed in ced-1 mutants is likely a result of a defect in signaling between phagosomes and autophagosomes.
source: Thus the recruitment defect observed in ced-1 mutants is not a consequence of the lack of autophagosomes; rather, it is likely a result of a defect in signaling between phagosomes and autophagosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that autophagosomes are present but not recruited to phagosomes in ced-1 mutants (Figure 9).

claim: In ced-6(n2095) and dyn-1(n4039) mutants, the median relative LGG-1 and LGG-2 signal intensities in the center of phagosomes are much lower than in wild-type samples at 50 min-post phagosome formation.
source: In the ced-6(n2095) and dyn-1(n4039) loss-of-function mutant embryos, the median relative LGG-1 and LGG-2 signal intensities in the center of phagosomes are much lower than that in wild-type samples, respectively, at 50 min-post phagosome formation mutants Figure 9B,D,F,G, K–L and Figure 10A, D E,F,I,J, although the defects are not as severe as in ced-1 mutants Figure 9A, C, F, G, K and L.
evidence: This is shown in Figures 9 and 10.

claim: In ced-6 and dyn-1 mutants, LGG-1 or LGG-2-labeled puncta are rarely observed on the surfaces of phagosomes, demonstrating severe defects in the recruitment of autophagosomes to phagosomal surfaces.
source: Further observation discovered that the LGG-1 or LGG-2-labeled puncta were rarely observed on the surfaces of phagosomes in these mutants Figure 9B,D1,J and Figure 10A, F, demonstrating severe defects in the recruitment of autophagosomes to phagosomal surfaces.
evidence: This is shown in Figures 9 and 10.

claim: In ced-5(n1812) and ced-10(n1993) mutants, the accumulation of LGG-1 and LGG-2 signals on phagosomal surfaces and inside phagosomal lumen is normal.
source: In these two mutants, the accumulation of the LGG-1 and LGG-2 signals on the surfaces of the phagosomes and the subsequent accumulation of signals inside phagosomal lumen were normal both in the time course and in the levels of signal enrichment (Figure 10B, C–E, G and H–J), indicating that both the recruitment and fusion of autophagosomes to phagosomes are normal.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 10B, C-E, G, and H-J.

claim: The CED-5/CED-10 pathway is not involved in regulating the incorporation of autophagosomes to phagosomes.
source: We thus conclude that, unlike the CED-1/–6 /DYN-1 pathway, the CED-5/–10 pathway is not involved in regulating the incorporation of autophagosomes to phagosomes (Figure 10K).
evidence: This is inferred from the normal autophagosome-phagosome fusion in ced-5 and ced-10 mutants (Figure 10).

claim: In wild-type embryos, NUC-1::mCherry puncta are first attached to phagosomal surfaces and subsequently the mCherry signal accumulates inside the phagosomal lumen.
source: In wild-type embryos, in phagosomes containing cell corpses C1, C2, and C3, we observed first the attachment of NUC-1::mCherry puncta on the surfaces of phagosomes and subsequently the accumulation of the mCherry signal inside the phagosomal lumen (Figure 11A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 11A.

claim: In lgg-1(tm3489), lgg-2(tm5755), and atg-7(bp411) embryos, numerous mCherry::NUC-1 puncta are enriched on phagosomal surfaces and subsequently fused to phagosomes.
source: In these mutants, numerous mCherry::NUC-1 puncta are enriched on the surfaces of phagosomes C1, C2, and C3 and are subsequently fused to phagosomes (Figure 11B–D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 11B-D.

claim: 60 min after phagosome formation, the average folds of increase of the luminal mCherry::NUC-1 signal in lgg-1, lgg-2, and atg-7 mutants are not significantly different from wild-type samples.
source: Quantitative analysis of 15 phagosomes for each genotype found that 60 min after phagosome formation, the average folds of increase of the luminal mCherry signal over the '0 min' time point in lgg-1, lgg-2, and atg-7 mutants are not significantly different from that observed from wild-type samples (Figure 11F).
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 11F.

claim: The median value of the first time point when NUC-1::mCherry signal is detected inside the phagosomal lumen is not significantly different in wild-type, lgg-1, lgg-2, and atg-7 genotypes.
source: In addition, the median value of the first time point when NUC-1::mCherry signal was detected inside the phagosomal lumen was not significantly different in all four genotypes (Figure 11G).
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 11G.

claim: The incorporation of lysosomes into phagosomes in lgg-1, lgg-2, and atg-7 mutants is as efficient as in wild-type embryos.
source: These data strongly suggest that the incorporation of lysosomes into phagosomes in lgg-1, lgg-2, and atg-7 mutants is as efficient as in wild-type embryos, at least within the detection range of our assay.
evidence: This is inferred from the quantitative data showing no significant difference in lysosome-phagosome fusion between wild-type and autophagy mutants (Figure 11F-G).

claim: Defects in the biogenesis of autophagosomes do not appear to significantly affect the incorporation of lysosomes into phagosomes.
source: Therefore, defects in the biogenesis of autophagosomes, which potentially would indirectly result in the lack of autolysosomes, do not appear to significantly affect the incorporation of lysosomes into phagosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing normal lysosome-phagosome fusion in autophagy mutants (Figure 11).

claim: In wild-type embryos, there are two kinds of mNG::LGG+ puncta recruited to phagosomal surfaces: those not labeled with NUC-1::mCherry (autophagosomes) and those labeled with NUC-1::mCherry (autolysosomes).
source: In the wild-type embryos that co-express the mNG::LGG-1 or –2 reporters with the NUC-1::mCherry reporter in engulfing cells, we observed that, in addition to the lysosomal particles that were mNG- but mCherry+, there were two kinds of mNG+ puncta that were recruited to phagosomal surfaces and subsequently fused to phagosomes. Those puncta that are not labeled with mCherry represent autophagosomes that are not fused to lysosomes; on the other hand, the mNG+ mCherry+ puncta represent autolysosomes (Figure 12A–B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 12A-B.

claim: 40.6% and 36.5% of LGG-1+ and LGG-2+ puncta on phagosomal surfaces are autolysosomes, respectively.
source: Quantification of these two kinds of puncta on the surfaces of the C1, C2, and C3 phagosomes reveals that 40.6% and 36.5% of LGG-1+ and –2+ puncta are autolysosomes, respectively (Figure 12C).
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 12C.

claim: The LGG+ NUC-1- population of autophagosomes are likely to deliver certain autophagosome-specific material to phagosomes.
source: Whereas the LGG+ NUC-1+ autolysosomes are capable of contributing both autophagosomal and lysosomal materials to phagosomes, the LGG+ NUC-1- population of autophagosomes are likely to deliver certain autophagosome-specific material to phagosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that a substantial fraction of LGG+ puncta on phagosomes are not labeled with the lysosomal marker NUC-1 (Figure 12).

claim: In atg-7(bp411) mutant embryos, there is a moderate phagosome acidification defect.
source: Compared to the cup-5 mutant embryos, in atg-7(bp411) null mutant embryos, we observed a moderate phagosome acidification defect (Figure 13C, D and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 13C, D, and E.

claim: The average acidification index values for wild-type, atg-7(bp411), and cup-5(n3264) mutants are 0.443, 0.679, and 0.912, respectively, at t = 51 min.
source: The average acidification index values for wild-type, atg-7(bp411), and cup-5(n3264) mutants are 0.443, 0.679, and 0.912, respectively, at t = 51 min.
evidence: This is calculated from the data shown in Figure 13.

claim: In atg-7(bp411) mutants, the acidification index values in 69.2% of phagosomes at t = 51 min are >0.6, yet the values of only 15.3% phagosomes are >0.9.
source: In atg-7(bp411) mutants, the acidification index values in 69.2% of the phagosomes at t = 51 min are >0.6, yet the values of only 15.3% phagosomes are >0.9.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 13E.

claim: The moderate acidification defect in atg-7 mutants is distinct from that observed in cup-5 mutants.
source: This moderate defect is distinct from that observed from the cup-5 mutants.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the acidification index distributions in atg-7 versus cup-5 mutants (Figure 13E).

claim: In wild-type embryos, the degradation of apoptotic cell chromatin DNA inside the phagosomal lumen allows the reduction of the size of the HIS-72::mCherry+ disc over time.
source: We observed that in the wild-type embryos, the degradation of the apoptotic cell-chromatin DNA inside the phagosomal lumen allowed the reduction of the size of the mCherry+ disc over time (Figure 14A and D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 14A and D.

claim: Within 60 min after phagosome formation in wild-type embryos, the average diameter of the HIS-72::mCherry+ disc reduces to 49% of the 0 min value.
source: Within 60 min after the formation of a phagosome, the average diameter of the mCherry+ disc reduces to 49% of the 0 min value (Figure 14E).
evidence: This is quantified and shown in Figure 14E.

claim: In cup-5(n3264) mutant embryos, within 60 min post phagosome formation, the average diameter of the HIS-72::mCherry+ disc remains at 89% of the 0 min-value.
source: We observed that, as predicted for a mutant severely defective in lysosomal biogenesis and functions, in cup-5(n3264) mutant embryos, within 60 min post phagosome formation, the average diameter of the mCherry+ disc remains at 89% of the 0 min-value (Figure 14B and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 14B and E.

claim: In atg-7(bp411) mutant embryos, within 60 min post phagosome formation, the average diameter of the HIS-72::mCherry+ disc is reduced to 66% of the 0 min-value.
source: In comparison, in atg-7(bp411) mutant embryos, that value is reduced to 66% of the 0 min-value; in addition, the diameters of the mCherry+ discs in 25% of the phagosomes are >80% of the 0 min-value.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 14E.

claim: In atg-7 mutants, there is a defect in the digestion of chromatin DNA, yet this defect is relatively moderate.
source: These results indicate that in atg-7 mutants, there is a defect in the digestion of chromatin DNA, yet this defect is relatively moderate.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the nuclear diameter reduction in atg-7 mutants versus wild-type and cup-5 mutants (Figure 14).

claim: A novel function of autophagosomes is facilitating the degradation of apoptotic cells through fusing to phagosomes.
source: We have identified a novel function of autophagosomes in facilitating the degradation of apoptotic cells through fusing to phagosomes.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by multiple lines of data (Figures 1-14).

claim: Through autophagosome-phagosome fusion, autophagosomes facilitate the degradation of apoptotic cells inside phagosomes, presumably through providing certain materials to phagosomes.
source: Through this previously unknown interaction, autophagosomes facilitate the degradation of apoptotic cells inside phagosomes, presumably through providing certain materials to phagosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that blocking autophagosome-phagosome fusion impairs phagosome degradation (Figures 5, 6, 13, 14).

claim: The signaling pathway led by CED-1 promotes the recruitment and subsequent fusion of autophagosomes to phagosomes.
source: We have further identified a signaling pathway that promotes the recruitment and subsequent fusion of autophagosomes to phagosomes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by data showing that CED-1, CED-6, and DYN-1 are required for autophagosome recruitment, and RAB-7 and the HOPS complex are required for fusion (Figures 8-10).

claim: This autophagosome-phagosome fusion mechanism might be conserved in metazoans and has a significant impact in the regulation of the immunological consequences of dying cells inside human bodies.
source: We propose that this mechanism might be conserved in the metazoans and has a significant impact in the regulation of the immunological consequences of dying cells inside human bodies.
evidence: This is speculation based on the evolutionary conservation of phagocytosis and autophagy mechanisms.

claim: In mammalian cells, besides LAP vesicles, canonical autophagosomes might also contribute to the degradation of apoptotic cells in phagosomes.
source: Based on the evolutionary conservation of almost all molecular mechanisms, in particular the strong conservation of the known mechanisms that control phagocytosis and autophagy in metazoans (Lu and Zhou, 2012; Zhang and Baehrecke, 2015), we propose that in mammalian cells, besides LAP vesicles, canonical autophagosomes might also contribute to the degradation of apoptotic cells in phagosomes.
evidence: This is speculation based on evolutionary conservation and the findings in C. elegans.
